newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. waiting for reply from Israel on mission.
newsitem.headline: U.N. waiting for reply from Israel on mission.

text.p: The United Nations has formally told Israel it wants to send a high-level official for the purpose of discussing its settlement policy and other issues, spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Thursday.

But Israel has not given its official reply to the proposed visit by Kieran Prendergast, a Briton, who is U.N. undersecretary-general for political affairs. U.N. officials indicated Israel would not be willing to accept a visit that concentrated on the settlements only.

Israeli press reports said the response to the visit would be negative but diplomats at Israel's mission to the United Nations stressed the issue was still being discussed in Jerusalem and they were expecting a response shortly.

An April 25 emergency special session of the U.N. General Assembly demanded an immediate halt to the construction of an Israeli settlement in East Jerusalem and called for an end to all assistance to "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories.
The resolution, adopted by 143 to 3 votes with 11 abstentions, asked Secretary-General Kofi Annan to "monitor the situation and to submit a report" within two months.
Eckhard, in reply to queries, said Annan on May 8 "wrote to Israel declaring his intention to send an envoy consistent with the General Assembly resolution" on the settlements.

"We have had discussions with the Israelis in New York but we have no formal response yet from them on this matter. Informally they have said they would welcome an envoy to discuss a wide variety of matters," he added.
